analysis.title: "Trick Or Treat": Goldman's Spooky Chart Pack Shows AI Credit Pricing In A 15% Drop For Hyperscaler Stocks
key_insights: Goldman's AI Credit Spreads index (GSUCHS30) and the hyperscaler credit index (GSXUHYPR) are at their widest levels of the year. The last time spreads were nearly this wide, the underlying hyperscaler equities were 15% lower than they are now.
Goldman's broad AI beneficiaries basket is down about 25% from its June high relative to the S&P 500 ex-AI.

Goldman's AI theme dashboard for the week: NeoClouds -24.8% over five days, Optical Networks -21.4%, Memory -16.6%. AI-at-Risk was the only theme with a meaningful gain, +3.5%. AI productivity names were insulated from tech.

Miller frames the debate as having moved from how much hyperscalers will spend to how they will pay for it: 'AI Capex has likely peaked and financing, sustainability, and returns on capital have become the debate rather than the next near term earnings revision.'
Hyperscaler capex growth peaked at 116% y/y in Q3 2026 per Goldman Investment Research. Consensus has it slowing every quarter through end-2027 to roughly 20%.

Goldman estimates hyperscaler capex (net of depreciation) added about 11 percentage points to S&P 500 EPS growth in 2026. That falls to 7pp in 2027 and -1pp in 2028 as depreciation from the data centers builds.

Market internals are weak: Friday had the second-highest put volume on record (behind June 2026), Goldman's sector/factor/industry-neutral Beta pair (GSP1BETA) is down 15% from its recent high, and High Beta Cyclicals broke their uptrend channel.
Cyclicals vs Defensives ex-commodities (GSP1CYDE) implies only 2% growth, down from 6% at the high. That is more pessimistic than the Atlanta Fed GDPNow of about 3.6%.
Hedge fund beta-adjusted net exposure is at the 67th percentile over five years while net leverage is at the 17th percentile, so funds are long more beta than leverage suggests.

Miller says valuation is not the problem: 'we wouldn't confuse skepticism and uncertainty with overvaluation. The NDX still trades at just 21x earnings.' He adds that financial conditions have shifted from a positive to a negative driver of growth, and the Debt Sensitive Equities basket (GSX1DEBT) is lagging as junk spreads widen.
Miller is not calling for a crash. He says the market is absorbing stress through rotation rather than index-level weakness, despite rising correlations and crowded positioning.

Trade 1, buy the broadening: the S&P 500 ex-AI (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P 500 by 586bps since Oct 6 and the correlation between AI and the rest of the market has turned negative. Hybrid structure: 18Dec26 SPXXAI >105%, 10y SOFR < ATMF CMS-0.30% at 9.5% (vs 28%/27% for the individual legs). In Europe the ex-Secular Themes basket (GSXESXXX) is up about 4.5% since Oct 1 vs a flat STOXX 600.

Trade 2, Quality with a caveat: the Quality pair (GSP1QUAL) is up 20% in three months to a 12-month high on about 13% realized vol, driven mostly by a selloff in the short leg. Miller warns RSI >80 implies scope for a sharp reversal if inflation/rates concerns ease. European Quality (GSPEQUAL) is up 7.5% in a month.

Trade 3, midterm healthcare: long ACA-Exposed Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), betting Democrats revive the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025, which would return patient volumes to providers.

Trade 4, Brazil: valuations are around mid-cycle, foreign participation is below prior election-cycle peaks, and positioning in rate-sensitive domestic stocks (GSBZRATE) is light. Miller sees upside into the Oct 25 runoff, with P/E re-rating from mid teens to high teens.

Trade 5, hedge Taiwan: TSMC fell 2.3% on a full-year guidance raise and accelerated capacity buildout. Hedge fund Taiwan positioning is at record levels while earnings fail to meet elevated expectations. Goldman's Asia desk is pushing shorts on Taiwan Semis (GSXATWSM) and Taiwan Tech ex-TSMC (GSXATTXT). Foreigners pulled a record ~$9.3B from Taiwanese stocks in a single day.

ZeroHedge commentary (not Goldman): hyperscaler CDS hit a fresh record, seven of 20 junk-rated AI data center bonds depend on CoreWeave as the single tenant, about $14B of distressed junk bonds back data centers whose only tenant is CoreWeave, and CoreWeave fell sharply the week of Oct 14. ZeroHedge says credit is pricing a move equities have not yet made.
Upcoming catalyst per ZeroHedge: Microsoft reports alongside the Fed decision on Oct 28.
